summary: Priority inversion in continuous batcher causing tenant-specific p99 latency spikes
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 ~09:10 UTC, NimbusPay reported sharp p95/p99 latency regressions for inference requests routed to their Dedicated pool in us-east. The regression appears correlated with recent continuous-batcher scheduler change that introduced fairness/priority weighting. Impact: p95 increased from ~85ms baseline to ~720ms and p99 up to 4.2s for NimbusPay tenant traffic; production user-facing timeouts (504s) rose from 0.01% to 0.9% for the affected endpoints. Not all tenants are affected; behavior seems tenant-specific and workload-sensitive (mixed short and long sequences). Environment: prod (us-east), dedicated capacity pool rn-dedicated-us-east-12 serving gpt-3.5-redwood-v1. Observed windows: 09:05–09:55 UTC. This is customer-impacting and on a paid dedicated tenant.

Immediate customer-visible symptoms: increased request latency tails, occasional 504 timeouts, and perceived instability of streaming sessions. Customer reported behavior after they rolled a mixed-length workload test (short prompts for routing logic + long generation for summaries).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a single tenant (NimbusPay) in the dedicated us-east pool. 2) Send a mixed workload: 70% short prompts (<= 8 tokens) and 30% long-generation prompts (~1024 tokens) at ~40-60 qps for 10 minutes. 3) Observe continuous-batcher metrics in /metrics (batcher_queue_depth, flush_latency, per-tenant weight) and request latencies in API telemetry. 4) Look for bursts where small requests wait multiple flush cycles (p99 spikes) while a few long requests occupy batcher worker lanes. Note: reproduces reliably when kv-cache miss rate for the tenant is >0.2 and the scheduler's per-tenant weight recalculation is enabled.

investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Root cause hypothesis: a priority inversion bug in the continuous-batcher/scheduler interaction. When KV-cache warmup activity spikes (high miss ratio) for a tenant, the weight recalculation logic can transiently assign a zero weight to that tenant under a specific code path introduced in PR 1287 (fair-share scheduling). Zero weight combined with a single-long-request occupying a worker leads to small short-lived requests being starved until the long worker finishes or the batcher rebalances.
- Evidence: scheduler debug logs show weight set to 0 immediately prior to observed p99 events; affected tenants correlate with higher cache-miss ratios; other tenants on same pool with similar QPS but lower miss ratios do not see the same spikes.
- Reproducibility: internal reproduction achieved in staging by forcing kv-cache misses and running the mixed workload (see steps_to_reproduce).
- Risk: medium-high for dedicated tenants using mixed-length workloads. This is not a universal regression but will surface for production traffic patterns that warm up KV caches or perform one-off heavy-generation requests.
- Temporary mitigation validated: pinning the tenant's route to a model-variant with pre-warmed cache reduces p99 to baseline; isolating long-running generation flows to a separate route also mitigates.

2026-03-12 09:50 - Ethan Park (Eng, serving-runtime): Reproduced locally in staging by forcing KV miss pattern. Root cause appears in fair-share weight recalculation when 'cache_warmup_inflight' > threshold. Attaching initial debug patch to block weight=0 assignment. See PR 1287 for recent scheduler change.

2026-03-12 10:05 - Maria Chen (Support) -> Customer (NimbusPay): Provided temporary workarounds: 1) pin to pre-warmed model variant; 2) split short routing traffic and long-generation traffic to separate endpoints. Customer applied pin and reported immediate reduction in p99.

2026-03-13 02:12 - Ethan Park (Eng): Deployed hotfix to canary that prevents zero-weight assignment during weight recompute. Monitoring Canary metrics; initial signs show p99 reduction for reproduced load. Planning rollback of the scheduler change in production if canary confirms.
resolution: Mitigation steps applied: 1) Hotfix deployed to canary to prevent zero-weight assignments (2026-03-13 02:00 UTC). 2) Advised customer to pin to pre-warmed variant or split workloads—customer reported immediate improvement. 3) Rollback window scheduled for the scheduler fair-share change if canary confirms hard failures. Follow-ups: create INT task to add unit/integration tests covering kv-cache miss + weight recompute path (INT-4421), add telemetry alert for per-tenant weight==0 events, and schedule postmortem runbook update. Permanent fix: scheduler logic will be patched to never assign zero weight and to prefer isolating KV-warmup flows into a separate low-priority lane. Target stable rollout: 2026-03-18 (dependent on test pass).
next_steps: 1) Continue canary monitoring for 24h (Ethan). 2) Create INT-4421 with detailed reproducible test case and link to PR 1287 (Ethan/Nora). 3) Contact NimbusPay CS lead with final RCA and ETA for permanent fix (Maria). 4) Add alert for 'per-tenant weight == 0' and 'batcher hold_time_ms > 2000' to avoid silent regressions (SRE).
